Subject: RFP SIG questionnaire + evidence cadence

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is CobaltEdge's SIG questionnaire (v2) for the RFP — it's detailed on controls mapping and we need a concise evidence schedule for our review board. Key asks from our side:

- High level control mapping (ISO/SOC equivalence) per section.
- For cryptographic and key management controls: we need provenance and escrow options (we require independent escrow for key escrow proofs for custodial scenarios).
- A list of representative artifacts (logs, configs, attestation excerpts) and expected delivery dates (we're targeting a complete package by 2026-10-15).
- Any deviations or compensating controls called out explicitly.

Can you confirm who will own this on your side and whether Redwood can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary and a sample KMS rotation log? Also note that our legal team will request an NDA amendment for escrow-related proofs.

Attaching: CobaltEdge_SIG_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx

Best,
Tom Reyes

CobaltEdge Capital

Subject: Re: RFP SIG questionnaire + evidence cadence — technical scope and timeline

Tom —

Following up with concrete asks and our proposed delivery windows. I reviewed the SIG and flagged the following priority controls where artifacts are commonly requested:

- Key Management (SIG 4.2 / CM-keys): We can provide a key rotation log (redacted to remove customer identifiers), KMS config export, and a short video walkthrough of KMS key policy. Target delivery: 2026-10-08.
- Access Control (SIG 3.x): IAM role snapshots and recent access review exports (redacted). Target delivery: 2026-10-06.
- Logging & Monitoring (SIG 6.x): Sample log bundle (30 days, scrubbed), alerting runbook, and pager rotation evidence. Target delivery: 2026-10-09.
- Change Management: PR/merge history crosswalk and change approval stamps. Target delivery: 2026-10-04.

Escrow note: independent escrow for key material is unusual but feasible for certain contractual models — we'll need your legal to define acceptable escrow agents and scope. Practically, the proofs we can supply without an escrow are: signed attestation of rotation events, HSM-export audit, and auditor-friendly key lineage report. With escrow we can provide timebound key material under escrow controls, subject to NDAs and proof-of-possession checks.

I've attached a short SOC2 overview that summarizes what we typically release for RFP reviews (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) — it's redacted for sensitivity.

Action items for us: Kimberly to deliver KMS and change-management artifacts (see dates above); Neha to prepare the SIG-control crosswalk by 10/04; Jonas to coordinate DocuSign for NDA amendment if escrow is requested.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Assurance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@cobaltedge.com>

Date: 2026-10-02T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP SIG questionnaire + evidence cadence

Kim/Jonas —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple clarifications from our side after a quick internal legal review:

- The board requires an option for an independent escrow for key proofs only if the deployment model includes Redwood-managed encryption keys. For BYOK we can accept auditor-signed attestation in lieu of physical escrow.
- Any video walkthroughs will need a summary transcript and a verifier checklist — we cannot accept video alone.
- Regarding log samples: please ensure time ranges exclude customer PII and provide a short schema map for the payload fields.

Tom is going to coordinate the NDA amendment request — legal prefers DocuSign, and we'll need a confidentiality addendum that covers escrow-proof handling. I'll loop in our security lead if we get into technical minutiae.
